what: The TikTok Caption Counter counts your caption the way TikTok does. It shows characters against the 4,000 limit (or 2,200, 150 or 80 if you prefer), plus hashtags, mentions, words, emojis and lines, with a bar that turns amber near the limit and red when you go over.
A phone preview shows your caption over a video frame with your username, bold hashtags and mentions, and the two-line cut-off before "more". You can add a frame from your video to see the real look.

Tips point out a long first line, missing or too many hashtags, repeated hashtags, hashtags broken by punctuation and too many mentions. One tap removes repeated hashtags, and you can copy the caption or only its hashtags.
uses: Make sure the caption fits before you post.
Check the first line is short enough to read before "more".
Check captions from Instagram or YouTube fit TikTok.
tutorial: Type or paste it in the box. It is saved on this device as you type.
Keep 4,000 for video captions, or pick 2,200, 150 or 80.
See characters, hashtags, mentions, words, emojis and lines.
See what shows in two lines and tap "more" to see the rest. Add a video frame if you like.
Fix anything marked with ! or ✕, and use "Remove repeated hashtags".
Press Copy caption, or Copy hashtags only.
features: Emojis count as you see them.
Characters, hashtags, mentions, words, emojis and lines.
Two-line cut-off with "more", your username and video frame.
Repeats, broken hashtags and how many you use.
Your draft caption stays when you come back.

example.title: Worked example: a cooking video caption
example.text: A creator pastes "POV: you finally learned to make perfect dumplings at home 🥟✨" followed by a line about the recipe, @chef.friend and seven hashtags. The counter shows 158 of 4,000 characters, 7 hashtags and 1 mention. The tips flag #cooking used twice and #self-care breaking at the hyphen. She taps "Remove repeated hashtags", changes it to #selfcare and copies the caption.

tips: Make the first line a hook; most people only read the first two lines.
Use a few specific hashtags that match the video.
Put hashtags at the end so the caption reads naturally.
Do not tag accounts that are not in the video.
problems: The count differs from another tool
Some tools count emojis as two or more characters. This tool counts them the way you see them, like TikTok.
A hashtag is not bold in the preview
It probably has a space or symbol after the #. Hashtags need letters or numbers straight after #.
It is kept in this browser only. Private windows do not keep it.
